Author: Al-Hidāyah was authored by Imām al-Marghīnānī, a distinguished Ḥanafī jurist from Central Asia. It is regarded as one of the most authoritative and widely studied works in the Ḥanafī school of Islamic jurisprudence.

Content: The work is a comprehensive legal manual that systematically expounds the principles and rulings of Ḥanafī fiqh. It covers a broad range of legal topics, including acts of worship, transactions, family law, and criminal law, presenting them with scholarly precision and depth.

Importance: Al-Hidāyah is a commentary on Bidāyat al-Mubtadī and serves as an essential guide for students and scholars seeking to understand the intricacies of Ḥanafī legal reasoning and rulings.

2. Bidāyah al-Mubtadī (بداية المبتدي)

Author: This foundational text was written by Imām al-Qudūrī, one of the most eminent jurists of the Ḥanafī school. It was composed as a concise introduction to Ḥanafī jurisprudence for beginners and students.

Content: Bidāyat al-Mubtadī presents essential legal rulings in a clear and simplified format, focusing on core aspects of fiqh without extensive legal argumentation.

Use: The text is widely taught to beginners in Ḥanafī jurisprudence and serves as a stepping stone to more advanced legal works, including Al-Hidāyah.

3. Fatḥ al-Qadīr (فتح القدير)

Author: Fatḥ al-Qadīr was authored by Imām Kamāl al-Dīn Ibn al-Humām, a leading Ḥanafī jurist and legal theorist.

Content: This work is an in-depth commentary on Al-Hidāyah, offering detailed analysis, clarification, and evidentiary discussion of its legal rulings. It engages with proofs, comparative opinions, and legal reasoning, making it a vital resource for advanced study.

Significance: When studied alongside Al-Hidāyah, Fatḥ al-Qadīr provides a fuller and more nuanced understanding of the Ḥanafī legal methodology, and is considered an indispensable reference for advanced students and scholars of Islamic law.

Among his esteemed teachers were giants such as Mawlānā Khalīl Aḥmad Sahāranpūrī, ʿAllāmah Shabbīr Aḥmad ʿUthmānī, and ʿAllāmah Anwar Shāh Kashmīrī. Distinguished as a scholar of ḥadīth and tafsīr, a poet, and an ascetic, he dedicated his life to the pursuit and teaching of the sacred sciences. He authored numerous important works in tafsīr, ḥadīth, and Islamic theology.

The Supreme Daily Remembrance (Al-Ḥizb al-A‘ẓam) – Bilingual Edition

Although several illuminated manuscripts of Al-Ḥizb al-A‘ẓam exist, no fully illuminated printed edition had been available until White Thread Press published one in 2015. For a book of prayers of such significance, illumination adds aesthetic beauty and enhances the reader’s spiritual engagement.

The English Translation 
Since the original Arabic edition, public recitals (maqra’āt) of the full collection have been held worldwide, often followed by authorization ceremonies (ijāzah) for attendees. These gatherings inspired many to become regular readers of the book. Responding to demand, White Thread Press now presents a bilingual edition, with the Arabic text and facing English translation in a clear, visually appealing format.

No effort has been spared to create an edition that brings immense joy and facilitates devotion.

Features of this edition include:

  • Arabic Typeface: Adapted from the original naskh script of the renowned Syrian calligrapher ‘Uthmān Ṭahā,** whose legible and elegant hand also prepared the Madīnah Mushaf read worldwide.

  • Layout: Twelve lines of Arabic per page with corresponding English translation, enclosed in a decorative gold-and-red frame.

  • Printing & Design: Five-color printing on coated, varnished stock; sewn pages for durability; bound to lie flat for easy reading.

  • Illumination & Ornamentation: Gold and colored headpieces mark the introduction and first section; section titles are enclosed in embellished borders. The ninety-nine Names of Allāh are featured across two double-page spreads. Ornaments indicate verse endings, and commas suggest pauses suited to the meaning, rhythm, and rhyme of invocations.

  • Typography & Navigation: Classical Arabic manuscript style with modern typographical touches, including page numbers and marginal section heads with numerals for easy navigation. Halfway markers help divide each of the seven sections for multi-day completion.

  • Translation: The English text is concise, lucid, and faithful to the eloquence of the Arabic, avoiding unnecessary words or expressions.

  • Textual Basis: Primarily based on Indian editions, compared and emended with manuscripts from around the world to ensure accuracy. Sections from Saturday to Tuesday follow most manuscripts, while remaining sections follow the Indian editions.

  • References & Appendices: Full references for invocations, a bibliography of print and manuscript sources, and an updated ijāzah for the author.

  • Deluxe Binding & Finishing: Front and back covers feature the book title in gold foil with a central medallion and the author’s name; a debossed frame and arabesque pattern highlight the spine; ribbon marker included; gold gilding on page edges.

Available in three faux leather covers:

  • Rustic Red

  • Rustic Blue

  • Textured Brown

This deluxe edition combines beauty, durability, and spiritual functionality, making it ideal for daily devotion and study.

name: Imam Abu Hanifa’s Al-Fiqh al-Akbar Explained
description:
Imām Abū Ḥanīfah’s Al-Fiqh al-Akbar Explained
By Abū ’l-Muntahā al-Maghnīsawī, with Selections from MullaʿAlī al-Qārī’s Commentary, including Abū Ḥanīfah’s Kitāb al-Wasiyyah*

Al-Fiqh al-Akbar is one of the earliest surviving works on Islamic creed (ʿaqīdah) and one of the foundational texts of Imām Abū Ḥanīfah, the eminent jurist and theologian. Studied for centuries across the Muslim world, this text offers a nuanced and layered understanding of Tawḥīd (divine oneness), the central tenet of Islamic belief. It sharpens comprehension of the Creator, the Prophets, and divine revelation, while providing insight into the realities of this life and the hereafter.

Beyond deepening one’s understanding of ʿaqīdah and nurturing spiritual conviction, Al-Fiqh al-Akbar addresses fundamental questions that, if left unresolved, could foster doubt or division within the community. Such questions include: Where is Allāh? Does Allāh undergo change? What constitutes true Islamic belief? Are Prophets capable of sinning? Does creation extend beyond what we perceive? What follows after death?

This English translation represents an unprecedented contribution to the study of Islamic creed. Rendered clearly and accessibly, it avoids overly literal or rigid translation, drawing on multiple commentaries to make a subject previously inaccessible to many English readers both intelligible and engaging. By combining Abū ’l-Muntahā al-Maghnīsawī’s commentary with extensive notes selected from ʿAlī al-Qārī’s super-commentary, and incorporating Abū Ḥanīfah’s complete Kitāb al-Wasiyyah, this edition serves as an essential guide for anyone undertaking an intellectual and rewarding journey through Islamic theology.
